## Dense helpers and the pivoted Gaussian solve (`dsolve_lu`) {#sec-ch10-dense}

### Summary

The per-cell solvers of kintera work on small dense matrices stored as plain row-major arrays. A set of helpers does
the vector and matrix products they need. One function, `dsolve_lu`, solves a square system by Gaussian elimination
with partial pivoting. It is the first solve of the implicit kinetics step and of the constrained Newton step, and
it reports an exactly singular matrix so that the caller can fall back to a least-squares solve.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Solve $\mathsf A x = b$ in place for a small dense $\mathsf A$, @eq-ch10-dense-elimination.

**Data.** Row-major $n \times n$ array and length-$n$ vector, destroyed and overwritten.

**Placement.** Inside per-cell kernels, on CPU or CUDA (@sec-ch12).

**Activation.** Always; no option.

**Guarantee / limits.** Fails only on an exactly zero pivot; no condition estimate.

**Evidence.** Indirect, through `test_thermo`; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf A$, an $n \times n$ matrix with entries $a_{ik}$; $b$, the right-hand side; $x$, the
solution; $k$, the elimination step; $f_{ik}$, the multiplier of row $i$ at step $k$.

### Derivation

At step $k$ the row with the largest $|a_{ik}|$, $i \ge k$, is swapped into row $k$ together with $b_k$. Then each
lower row is reduced:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{ik} &= a_{ik} / a_{kk} \\
a_{ij} &\leftarrow a_{ij} - f_{ik}\, a_{kj} \\
b_i &\leftarrow b_i - f_{ik}\, b_k
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-dense-elimination}

for $i > k$ and $j > k$. Back substitution then gives, for $i = n-1$ down to $0$,

$$
x_i = \frac{1}{a_{ii}} \Big( b_i - \sum_{j > i} a_{ij}\, x_j \Big) .
$$ {#eq-ch10-dense-back}

@eq-ch10-dense-elimination and @eq-ch10-dense-back are computed in `dsolve_lu`
({{< code src/math/core.h dsolve_lu >}}). The method is exact in exact arithmetic; its rounding error is that of
partial-pivoting elimination, not derived here.

### Numerical method

The elimination runs column by column with no scaling of rows. A column whose largest remaining magnitude is exactly
zero ends the solve with `false`; any nonzero pivot, however small, is accepted. The multipliers are not stored, so
the factorization cannot be reused for another right-hand side. The figure is not provided: the figure module is not
written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| pivoted solve | {{< code src/math/core.h dsolve_lu >}} | `dsolve_lu` | always |
| products | {{< code src/math/core.h mmdot >}} | `mmdot` | always |
| matrix-vector product | {{< code src/math/core.h mvdot >}} | `mvdot` | always |
| $\mathsf A^{\mathrm T} \mathsf A$ | {{< code src/math/core.h matmul_ATA >}} | `matmul_ATA` | always |
| swaps | {{< code src/math/swap.h swap_cols_safe >}} | `swap_cols_safe` | always |

: Code map of the dense helpers. {#tbl-ch10-dense-code}

1. `core.h` also holds `set_identity`, `vvdot`, `norm2`, `normalize`, `mvdot_t` and `mmdot_t`; `swap.h` holds
   `swap_cols`, `swap_cols_safe`, `swap_vals` and `swap_rows`. All are templates marked for host and device.
2. The implicit kinetics step of @sec-ch06 builds $\mathsf I/\Delta t - \mathsf S \mathsf J$ with `mmdot` and calls
   `dsolve_lu`; if it returns `false`, the step falls back to `psolve` of @sec-ch10-pseudo-inverse
   ({{< code src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h >}}).
3. `constrained_newton_step` of @sec-ch10-newton calls `dsolve_lu` first.

### Limits

- `mmdot_t` does not compute $\mathsf a\,\mathsf b^{\mathrm T}$: its inner sum reads `a[i * n2 + j] * b[j * n2 + k]`,
  with `j` where `k` belongs ({{< code src/math/core.h mmdot_t >}}). It has no caller outside `src/math` at the pin,
  so no result depends on it (searched in `src`, `python` and `tests`).
- `swap_cols` carries the comment "no-op trick won't work; do normal swap" next to a comma expression. Read under
  C++17 sequencing rules, the expression does swap the two columns; this is a hypothesis, not tested. It has no
  caller; `psolve` uses `swap_cols_safe` ({{< code src/math/swap.h swap_cols >}}).
- `swap_rows` takes a row count `m` that it does not use.
- `set_identity`, `vvdot`, `norm2`, `normalize`, `mvdot_t`, `swap_cols`, `swap_rows` and `swap_vals` have no caller
  outside `src/math` at the pin (searched by name; `normalize` also matches unrelated words).
- `dsolve_lu` gives no warning for a nearly singular matrix.
